title: Iran 'behind US tech outages' as expert claims cyberattacks causing chaos
excerpt: The expert made a bombshell claim.
content_html:
The expert made a bombshell claim.

17:51, Tue, Nov 17, 2026 Updated: 18:22, Tue, Nov 17, 2026

Flights were grounded last week (Image: Getty)

Iran is likely behind the tech outages that have plunged the US into chaos in recent days, an expert has claimed. The digital and physical world is still reeling after cyber criminals targeted 178 popular global websites in a bid to steal credit card details and infect iPhones.

Hackers injected malicious code through the web optimisation platform Optimizely, which is used by many companies to test changes to their websites. Some of the popular sites, which use Optimizely, impacted by this cyberattack include the BBC, FOX News, IKEA, Zoom and HSBC.

In the US major banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, reported trouble accessing services. Chase bank said its problem was now resolved. The online nightmare also hit travellers with United Airlines reporting a "widespread system outage" after Microsoft also was hit by problems. Concerning the grounding of flights in the US, officials blamed an upgrade to the decades-old telecoms network.

But US intelligence veteran Andrew Badger told LBC he believed the White House was downplaying the real culprit behind the back-to-back online meltdowns.

‘I think the Trump administration is downplaying this.’Grey-zone warfare expert Andrew Badger tells @TomSwarbrick1 why he suspects Iran is behind America's latest wave of Microsoft, banking and aviation outages. https://t.co/SXR4ZR192k

— LBC (@LBC) November 17, 2026

Mr Badger told the broadcaster he thought we are "in the middle of a massive grey-zone warfare campaign". So-called grey-zone warfare is the term used to describe states acting against one another without open conflict.

Examples can include; cyber warfare and disruption of critical infrastructure, espionage and sabotage, economic pressure, trade restrictions, or undermining supply chains and information warfare, propaganda, and election interference.

"We have to put forward multiple hypotheses about who could be behind this," Mr Badger said.

"I think the reason will show that Iran behind this threat. It's looking at the important context here. President Trump just a third aircraft carrier into the Perian Gulf, 2,000 marines who are ready at a moment's notice, we have 13 destroyers."

Andrew Badger said he believed Iran could be behind recent cyber attacks (Image: Getty)

Mr Badger said his hypothesis is that the recent cyber disruption was "Iran lashing out".

He added: "Iran lashing out... basically signalling to the Trump administration, trying to change its cost-benefit analysis that if you attack us again, we will hit you hard, we will hit you at home, and this is what every adversary of the United States has ever known, the political will of the American public is our true vulnerability and they're trying to break that will.

"I think the Trump administration is not being honest by the way, about who is behind these attacks."
